references.author: Adunni Olorisha Trust / Adunni Osun Foundation
references.observation: The First Palace is the central Ọ̀ṣun shrine. The front has a shallow corrugated main roof, a projecting timber gable, carved posts and irregular deep openings. The walls behind the porch carry painted decoration. The foundation has an uneven, green-weathered skirt, and some porch posts are lighter and more worn than others. The wider frontal photo shows the exposed corrugated roof. The roof revision carries the metal beneath the uneven straw boundary visible in the flyover.

references.author: Cheeka 2.0
references.observation: Street-level photograph shows steps, carved timber posts under the gable, and three deep window-like openings on the right side.

references.author: Ayodeji Daniel
references.observation: The photographer describes the pictured altar as being in front of the palace. The tagged position and bearing describe the camera aimed at the altar. They constrain the search area for the palace and leave the building center and façade bearing unresolved.

references.author: Adunni Olorisa Trust
references.observation: The overhead sequence at 0:11–0:31 shows a rectangular open court, roofs on the four sides and a separate curved canopy within the court. Sparse straw crosses the main gable and wraps over the edges. Near 0:35, corrugated metal is visible below the thatch at the entrance. The modeled exposed strip and corrugations follow the visible layering. Their dimensions are estimated.

references.author: CyArk / Adunni Olorisha Trust
references.observation: The interior view shows two differently sculpted front supports at the courtyard canopy and a smaller figure beside the right support. Behind the posts, a dark, roughly rectangular doorway sits beneath a gable wall and opens at the worn paving. The model follows the visible profile, with a shallow recess, side reveals and a stone threshold. Slab outlines, doorway depth and wall dimensions are estimates.

references.author: Adunni Olorisha Trust / Adunni Osun Foundation
references.observation: A cord dips between the recessed carved posts and carries a loose fringe. The stone steps have rounded uneven front edges and moss-darkened risers. The lower entrance remains open. The projecting plaster around the doorway has two unequal shoulders. The left spreads broadly into the stone approach and has moss below the carved posts. The narrower right side sweeps back into the window wall.

The published image looks directly at the carved gable, rose plaster window wall and stone steps. A dark iron grille closes the recessed doorway behind the porch. Long uneven fibers hang along the right wing over the corrugated edge.

references.author: Yngshot
references.observation: A second view shows faded rose plaster around the courtyard entrance wing and its right-hand openings.

map.result: The September 2024 geotagged entrance photo constrains the west-facing placement to about 265° true. Alternative photo controls give about 252°–268°, and the phone reports 4.8 m horizontal position uncertainty. The reconstructed footprint lies clear of the PMTiles road and river. A bounded grade exposes the lowest step and supports the documented court without moving the sampled road or river. The precise footprint and grade remain approximate.

firstPalaceControl.basis: Figure 1 marker 8 and the geotagged photograph of the nearby altar identify the wooded search area on the inside of the river bend.

limitations: The EXIF bearing is the optical direction. Model-relative camera orientation comes from approximate architectural controls.
The range describes the tested variation in the controls and focal length. The survey error is unknown.
The oriented envelope and bounded grade provide an approximate placement at the photographed site. Its survey footprint and grade remain unavailable.

grille.observation: Narrow iron scroll panels flank the straight central grid in the street and close-up tiers. Their proportions follow the two front photographs. Individual curls and bar spacing are reconstructed.

limitations: The First Palace includes the courtyard and covered galleries seen in the shrine trust’s aerial footage. The gallery dimensions, flat review floor and door connection are reconstructed.

The entrance roof wings expose corrugated metal beneath the straw. The exact material boundary, finer wall paintings and carvings are interpreted. The grove’s gates, forest and separate shrines have their own catalog records.

The entrance fringe follows the Trust photograph. The cord and individual strand lengths are reconstructed, and the current arrangement is unverified.
The flared entrance jambs follow their visible silhouette. Their dimensions and the depth of the plaster moldings are estimates.
The 2024 entrance photo shows faded rose plaster, a recessed iron grille and hanging fibers on the right eave. The exact grille spacing, fiber lengths and finish colors are estimated.

The courtyard photographs show the worn stone around the canopy and a dark recessed doorway between the carved supports. Slab outlines, the recess dimensions and the courtyard grade are estimated. The deeper sanctuary is out of view.
